--- title: "EIR and HBR" --- Where only entomological data are available, the pipeline is entered at HBR and prevalence is not used at all, and for that case `estimint` bundles a model in each direction. ::: {#b1952aa1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd from estimint import load_xgb_model, run_xgb_model eir_to_hbr = load_xgb_model("eir_to_hbr") # eir -> HBR hbr_to_eir = load_xgb_model("hbr") # hbr_y9 -> EIR eir_to_hbr["features"], hbr_to_eir["features"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['eir', 'dn0_use', 'Q0', 'phi_bednets', 'seasonal', 'itn_use', 'irs_use'], ['dn0_use', 'Q0', 'phi_bednets', 'seasonal', 'itn_use', 'irs_use', 'hbr_y9']) ``` ::: ::: Both take the same six setting covariates as the prevalence model, and they differ only in the driving column, `eir` for `eir_to_hbr` and `hbr_y9` for `hbr`. The model named `"hbr"` takes an HBR as its *input*, and it returns an EIR. ## From EIR to HBR Continuing the setting from [Estimating EIR from prevalence](estimating-eir.qmd), where a prevalence of 0.30 implied an EIR of about 13.4. ::: {#73bda3e6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} setting = dict( dn0_use=0.33, Q0=0.87, phi_bednets=0.82, seasonal=0.0, itn_use=0.6, irs_use=0.0, ) prev_model = load_xgb_model("prevalence") eir = run_xgb_model(pd.DataFrame([{**setting, "prevalence": 0.30}]), prev_model)[0] hbr = run_xgb_model(pd.DataFrame([{**setting, "eir": eir}]), eir_to_hbr)[0] f"eir = {eir:.2f}, hbr = {hbr:,.0f}" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 'eir = 13.40, hbr = 238,819' ``` ::: ::: Across the training data, HBR spans roughly `5e3` to `7e7`, which is four orders of magnitude against an EIR range of tens to hundreds, so the `hbr` model treats its input on a **log scale** internally, sweeping `hbr_y9` log-spaced rather than linearly. A linear treatment would spend almost all its resolution on the top decade and none where most districts sit. ## From HBR back to EIR If a trap gives a biting rate directly, this is the only model needed. The biting rate enters as `hbr_y9` and an EIR comes back. That EIR goes straight to the emulator. ::: {#0a20aced .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} back = run_xgb_model(pd.DataFrame([{**setting, "hbr_y9": hbr}]), hbr_to_eir)[0] f"eir = {back:.2f}" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 'eir = 14.23' ``` ::: ::: ## The round trip does not close The round trip starts at a prevalence of 0.30, converts that to an EIR, converts the EIR to an HBR, and converts the HBR back to an EIR. ::: {#9e0c4bc1 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} trip = pd.DataFrame([{ "prevalence": 0.30, "eir (from prevalence)": eir, "hbr (from eir)": hbr, "eir (from hbr)": back, "ratio": back / eir, }]) trip.round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
prevalence eir (from prevalence) hbr (from eir) eir (from hbr) ratio
0 0.3 13.397 238818.554 14.232 1.062
``` ::: ::: The EIR that comes back is about 6% higher than the one that went out. The two models were fitted separately, each with its own smoothing, and nothing constrains one to be the exact inverse of the other. Composing them combines the error of both. At 6%, a single conversion is still useful and a chain of them is not, which gives two rules. Do not round-trip, because where a prevalence is available the EIR from the prevalence model is the estimate, and converting onward to HBR and back does not refine it but degrades it. Do not compare a prevalence-derived EIR with an HBR-derived EIR as though they were on the same footing. They carry different biases, and a difference of a few percent between them says more about the models than about the districts. ::: {.callout-note} ## The gap is why the density method uses a ratio This gap is why [`estimate_eir_with_mosquito_delta`](mosquito-density.qmd) never uses a round-tripped EIR as an answer. It predicts the EIR at *both* the baseline HBR and the changed HBR, and keeps only the **ratio** of the two, in which the bias is common to the numerator and to the denominator. It cancels. The ratio is then applied to a baseline EIR taken straight from the prevalence model, which never went near the HBR models. ::: `hbr_y9` is clamped to `[5e3, 7e7]`, silently, in the same way `prev_y9` is clamped to `[0.005, 0.80]`. A biting rate below five thousand returns the EIR for five thousand. ## Next - [Mosquito density and EIR](mosquito-density.qmd) — the ratio method, applied. - [EIR, HBR, prevalence, and cases](../03-concepts/equilibrium.qmd) — why these are equilibrium values and not trajectories.
